Run Tools Reference ​

Every Run gives PRIME a small, fixed toolbelt. These nine tools are the only way PRIME can change a Run: set its contract, dispatch work, ship a branch, raise an event, or close it out. They are exposed as an in-process MCP server named saidi_run, so their fully-qualified names are mcp__saidi_run__<tool>.

The toolbelt below is the canonical list.

ToolPurposeMutates the Run?
set_planFreeze the Run's task contractYes — once
amend_planChange the frozen plan, with a reasonYes
delegateHand one task to one agentYes
delegate_batchRun 2–8 independent tasks concurrentlyYes
get_run_stateRead the durable plan backNo — read-only
publishPush a project's run branch and open a PRYes — remote
raise_eventEmit an event onto the reflex busYes — may start other Runs
attach_assetsAttach generated files into the Run chatYes — chat only
finish_runClose the Run once its objective is metYes — terminal

A recurring theme runs through all of them: the tools refuse rather than comply when the Run's contract would be violated. A refusal comes back as an MCP error result with an explanation, and PRIME has to deal with it. See Verification & Evidence for why the gates exist.

Planning tools ​

set_plan ​

Sets the Run's task plan. PRIME calls this once, on its first turn, before delegating anything. The plan becomes the Run's contract — what the Run is measured against and what finish_run later checks.

Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredNotes
itemsPlanItem[]YesThe full task list, in order. Minimum 1, maximum 12.

The PlanItem shape

FieldTypeRequiredMeaning
idstringOptionalShort stable id, e.g. "api", "ui", "verify". Preserved across amendments. Generated if omitted.
textstringYesOne concrete step, short.
assigneestringOptionalAgent or project responsible for this task.
dependsOnstring[]OptionalTask ids that must be done first.
mode"ask" | "work"OptionalRead-only Q&A vs. change-making.
effort"low" | "medium" | "high"OptionalReasoning tier. low for simple read-only lookups, medium for normal audit/build/verification work, high only for unusually hard judgment or design.
attemptBudgetinteger ≥ 1OptionalRetries this task may use before the Run escalates. Clamped to the configured maximum — a plan cannot raise its own ceiling.
acceptanceCriteriastring[]Yes1–5 observable conditions for completion.
checksCheck[]OptionalMechanical assertions. Max MAX_TASK_CHECKS.
proofsProof[]OptionalDeterministic evidence. Max 5.

acceptanceCriteria is mandatory and is enforced. Each entry must be something a checker can rule on: a file that must exist, a command that must pass, a count, an output that must contain a specific thing. "it looks good" is rejected. Criteria should be scoped to the symptom in the brief, not an exhaustive survey of the surrounding subsystem.

The Check shape — one mechanical assertion each, judged only by exit code.

FieldTypeMeaning
cmdstringShell command, capped at MAX_CHECK_CMD_CHARS.
expectExitintegerExit code that means passed. Default 0.
criterionstringWhich acceptance criterion this proves — set it to the criterion's exact text.

Checks are deliberately weak-by-design in one direction and strong in the other: a failing check fails the task outright, but a passing check does not complete it. PRIME wrote both the criteria and the checks, so the verifier still rules on every criterion independently. Checks make the gate stricter, never weaker. They may only run inspection commands — test, grep, npm/npx, read-only git — with no writes, no network, and no node -e. The assigned agent is shown them in its brief.

The Proof shape — closed-vocabulary deterministic evidence, preferred over asking a worker to paste files or raw build logs inline.

FieldTypeMeaning
criterionstringExact acceptance-criterion text this proves.
kind"fileExists" | "assetCount"The proof type.
pathstringSafe relative path, for fileExists.
minCountinteger ≥ 1Minimum matching run assets, for assetCount.
extensionstringOptional extension filter such as .png.

Refusals

  • Calling set_plan when a plan already exists returns an error directing PRIME to amend_plan instead — silently replacing the plan "is how a run ends up somewhere different every time it is run".
  • A plan failing validation returns Plan rejected: followed by the specific problems.

On success the plan is normalized, stored, and frozen. If the Run requires plan approval, the plan is not dispatched: its approval state is set to pending, a question event is posted to the operator listing each task with its criteria, and PRIME is told to stop and wait. This is the checkpoint for "is this the right work" — distinct from verification, which answers the later question "was it actually done".

text
Plan set and frozen (5 tasks). It is now this run's contract — change it only with
amend_plan, stating why.

amend_plan ​

Changes a frozen plan, on the record. Every amendment appends a system event noting the reason and the drift since the original plan — how many tasks were added, removed, and reworded.

Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredNotes
reasonstringYesMinimum 8 characters. Why the plan must change — what reality turned out to be different.
itemsPlanItem[]YesThe full revised task list, in order, 1–12 items. Same shape as set_plan.

Pass the entire list every time and preserve existing ids.

What an amendment may not do

  • It cannot drop or reopen a task that is already done.
  • It cannot remove a task's acceptance criteria.
  • It cannot set task status. Status belongs to the engine — an amendment cannot mark work done.
  • It cannot be called before a plan exists; you get There is no plan to amend yet — call set_plan first.

Legitimate reasons are narrow: the work turned out to need a step nobody knew about, or a step turned out not to apply. Because every amendment is recorded, the incentive is to get the plan right in set_plan.

A rejected amendment returns Amendment rejected: with the specific problems. A successful one returns the new plan version and task count.

get_run_state ​

Reads the Run's durable plan back from the store. Read-only, so it is always safe to call.

Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredNotes
taskIdsstring[]OptionalOnly these task ids. Omit for the whole plan.
includeEvidencebooleanOptionalInclude each task's latest evidence. Default true.

Each Run turn already carries a live-state block listing every open task, which covers the normal case. get_run_state exists for the two cases it cannot cover:

  1. A plan longer than the live-state block displays.
  2. A PRIME whose session was just compacted and needs the criteria and evidence behind a task — not just its status.

Returns a plan version header with a done/total count, then one block per task containing id, status, assignee, attempt number, task text, acceptance criteria, the verification verdict (status, who ruled, and reason), and the latest evidence clipped to 1,200 characters.

text
Plan v2 — 3/5 done.

### api — done · corex · attempt 1
Add the /health endpoint
Criteria:
- GET /health returns 200
Verdict: pass (by verifier)
Evidence: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" … → 200

Errors if the Run no longer exists, if no task matches the supplied ids, or if the Run has no plan yet.

Delegation tools ​

delegate ​

Hands one piece of the Run to a project or department agent. The agent streams live into the Run thread and its task status updates automatically.

Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredNotes
targetstringYesProject registry name or custom agent name.
taskstringYesPrecisely what the agent should do or answer.
mode"ask" | "work"Optionalask is read-only repo Q&A; work may run commands or make a change on the run branch.
taskIdstringOptionalStable id of the matching set_plan item — this is what links the delegation to the checklist.
approvedbooleanOptionalSet true only after the owner explicitly approved this exact change.

approved is the approval-gate carrier. It is not a convenience flag: it asserts that a human signed off on this specific change, and project policy decides whether that assertion is required. See Project Policy and Approval & Spend Guardrails.

Always pass taskId. Without it the delegation is orphaned from the plan, and nothing updates the checklist item it was meant to satisfy.

delegate_batch ​

Runs 2–8 independent, ready checklist tasks concurrently.

Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredNotes
tasksobject[]YesMinimum 2, maximum 8 items.
tasks[].targetstringYesProject registry name or custom agent name.
tasks[].taskstringYesPrecisely what this agent should do or answer.
tasks[].mode"ask" | "work"Optionalask for read-only repo Q&A, work otherwise.
tasks[].taskIdstringYesRequired here, unlike in delegate.

Note the one schema difference from delegate: taskId is required for every batch item, and there is no approved field — approval-gated work cannot be batched at all.

The five preconditions, each with its own refusal

ConditionRefusal
Duplicate taskIds in the batchdelegate_batch requires a distinct taskId for every item.
A taskId not present in the planUnknown checklist taskId(s): …. They must exist in the plan.
A task whose dependsOn entries are not yet doneNot batching: dependencies are still open for ….
Two items resolving to the same canonical agent/projectdelegate_batch requires distinct agents/projects. Work aimed at the same target must be sequenced with delegate.
A work-mode project task whose policy approval is confirmApproval-gated work cannot start in a batch: …. Delegate those tasks individually.

Targets are resolved to their canonical registry names before the duplicate check, so two different aliases for the same project are still caught.

Failure isolation. The batch settles all delegations rather than aborting on the first error. Successful results are preserved when a sibling fails, and each checklist task receives its own final status. The combined result is only marked as an error if every item failed. Results come back as one block per item, headed ### <taskId> · <target>.

The batch also short-circuits before doing anything if the Run was stopped, or if the account's usage limit is blocking work — see Credits, Usage & Spend Limits.

Output tools ​

publish ​

Publishes a project's run branch: pushes it to origin and opens a pull request.

Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredNotes
targetstringYesProject registry name whose run branch to publish.

This tool exists because run work does not push by itself. Changes accumulate as local commits on the run branch, and publishing is a deliberate, separate step taken when the owner wants them shipped. See Worktrees, Branches & Publishing.

Refuses if the Run was stopped. Otherwise returns whatever the publish attempt reported, flagged as an error if it did not succeed.

attach_assets ​

Attaches generated files from the Run's assets folder directly into the Run chat. It does not rerun work and does not modify repo files.

Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredNotes
filesstring[]OptionalSpecific filenames from the Run assets folder. Omit to attach every unattached generated asset.
includeAlreadyAttachedbooleanOptionalNormally false. Set true only if the owner explicitly wants duplicates or a re-send.
notestringOptionalShort message or caption shown above the attached files.

Two situations call for it: the owner asks to send or show generated images, screenshots, PDFs, or exports in the chat; or a restart left files in the assets folder without chat attachments.

raise_event ​

Emits a Saidi event onto the reflex bus from inside the Run.

Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredNotes
typestringYesEvent type, e.g. "lead.captured" or "incident.detected".
payloadRecord<string, unknown>OptionalNormalized fields other reflexes can match on.

Use it when the Run discovers something actionable that a Reflex should react to — start a run, notify someone, chain further work. A lead was captured; an incident was detected; a threshold was crossed.

The emitted envelope fixes several fields for you:

FieldValue
source"agent"
actorThe Run's title
runIdThe current Run's id
depth1
atEmission timestamp
idA fresh event id

depth is the loop guard: events raised from inside a Run are depth-guarded so a reflex that starts a run that raises an event cannot recurse indefinitely. Refuses if the Run was stopped.

See Reflexes & Events and Reflex Rules.

finish_run ​

Closes the Run. PRIME calls it when the Run's objective is fully met.

Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredNotes
notestringOptionalOne-line outcome summary.
evidencestringOptionalWhat was verified and how — a build or test that passed, a check an agent ran. Not just what was done.

Completion is a contract, not a claim. finish_run applies two independent gates before it will close anything.

Gate 1 — no open plan steps. If any task is still open, the tool refuses and lists them:

text
Not finishing: 2 plan steps are still open:
- Add the /health endpoint (in_progress)
- Update the deploy doc (pending)
Complete them, or amend_plan with a reason if a step genuinely no longer applies (and tell
the owner why).

Gate 2 — nothing "done" that went unverified. A Run's executionMode is either guided or autonomous. When verification is active for that mode, any task marked done that nothing actually checked is refused:

text
Not finishing: 1 step completed without passing verification:
- Add the /health endpoint
Re-delegate them so their acceptance criteria are actually checked.

This second gate is the point of the whole design: a task marked done that nothing verified is precisely the claim the layer exists to stop accepting at face value.

On success the Run is marked complete and, if a note or evidence was supplied, a ✔ system event is appended to the thread. The owner can still reopen a closed Run.

finish_run is not a way out of a stuck Run. If more work or a decision from the owner remains, PRIME is instructed to say what is left and let the owner steer, rather than closing.

Behaviour common to all run tools ​

  • Stopped runs. Tools that dispatch or mutate remote state — delegate, delegate_batch, publish, raise_event — check the abort signal first and return The run was stopped.
  • Usage blocking. Delegation paths call the usage gate before dispatching. If the account is blocked, the tool returns the block message instead of starting work.
  • Result clipping. Tool output returned to PRIME is clipped to a cap so a single verbose agent cannot consume the whole context. Batch results share the cap across items with a per-item floor, and clipped content carries a pointer for recovering the detail via the agent.
  • Text segmentation. PRIME's own prose is segmented by tool call — each contiguous stretch of text between delegations becomes its own message in the thread, which is why the transcript reads as narration interleaved with work rather than one wall of text.
